lessons.title: What To Expect
lessons.description: Learn what this workshop covers and how it will help you build a local AI workflow that fits your own hardware and use cases.

lessons.title: Basic Install
lessons.description: Install LM Studio and run a small local model so you have a working setup before we explore the details.

lessons.title: Why Choose Local AI?
lessons.description: Learn when local models make sense, where cloud frontier models are stronger, and why local AI skills matter to companies.

lessons.title: What Is a Model
lessons.description: Learn what a model is, how neural networks use weights and parameters, and why open weights are just files full of numbers.

lessons.title: What Makes LLMs Special
lessons.description: See how language becomes tokens, how an LLM predicts text one token at a time, and how context and sampling settings affect its output.

lessons.title: How LLMs Run On Hardware
lessons.description: Learn how CPUs, GPUs, RAM, VRAM, and unified memory affect whether a local model fits and how quickly it can generate text.

lessons.title: Model Families and Naming
lessons.description: Learn how to read a model name and what model families are.

lessons.title: Finding Models On Hugging Face
lessons.description: Learn how to search Hugging Face, evaluate a model repository, and identify the right files to download.

lessons.title: Model Types By Task
lessons.description: Learn the common types of AI models and how to choose one that matches the task you want to perform.

lessons.title: Dense Models, MoE, And MTP
lessons.description: Learn what dense models, mixture-of-experts models, and multi-token prediction mean for local model performance.

lessons.title: Model Formats And Runtimes
lessons.description: Learn why model files need a compatible runtime and how formats such as GGUF and MLX affect a local setup.

lessons.title: Matching Models To Your Hardware
lessons.description: Learn which hardware details affect local models and how we will use them to find compatible models on Hugging Face.

lessons.title: Understanding Quantization
lessons.description: See how quantization reduces model memory use, why names such as Q4 and Q8 matter, and how to choose a first download.

lessons.title: Will This Model Fit?
lessons.description: Estimate a model's memory needs before downloading it, then verify the estimate with a controlled load test.

lessons.title: Model Configuration
lessons.description: Learn how to read a model card for the prompt template, chat template, and generation settings a local model expects.

lessons.title: Measuring Local Inference
lessons.description: Learn which local-model performance metrics matter and how to compare models without changing every variable at once.

lessons.title: LM Studio API Mode
lessons.description: Learn how LM Studio turns a loaded local model into an OpenAI-compatible API that developer tools can use.

lessons.title: Configuring Developer Tools
lessons.description: Learn the shared configuration pattern for connecting an editor, CLI, or coding agent to LM Studio.

lessons.title: VS Code And Agent Mode
lessons.description: Connect VS Code to LM Studio in both Agent mode and regular chat mode.

lessons.title: Connecting Pi
lessons.description: Configure Pi to use LM Studio models.

lessons.title: Remote Access Overview
lessons.description: Learn when remote access makes sense and choose between LM Link and a manual Tailscale connection without exposing your model server publicly.

lessons.title: Remote Models With LM Link
lessons.description: Use LM Link to make a model loaded on another computer available through your local LM Studio server.

lessons.title: Remote Access With Tailscale
lessons.description: Connect a client to an LM Studio server over a private Tailscale network.

lessons.title: Running Models In The Cloud
lessons.description: Rent a more powerful machine to run your own local model server when buying new hardware does not make sense yet.
